verdict.rationale: Perplexity's own docs describe an official hosted MCP server that exposes Computer's core agent capabilities programmatically. It supports task delegation with structured results and continuing threads via thread_id. It also handles progress notifications, 200 MB file uploads, approving sensitive actions, relaying clarification answers, and auth_required flows. The documented capability list covers web and browser tasks, the sandboxed VM, document creation, deploys, email and calendar, and 400+ connectors. A separate org Analytics API exists, and runtime probes confirm the OAuth-protected endpoint is live. Nothing in the evidence claims UI–API parity: it is a single delegation tool reached over MCP/OAuth rather than a full REST surface. Account-side UI functions such as managing connectors, settings and task history are not shown as API-accessible. missing for 10: an explicit parity commitment or a full REST/OpenAPI surface for Computer, API coverage of UI management functions (connectors, settings, task listing/history), independent hands-on corroboration of API-driven use.
